results.controlIntent: (a) In accordance with [Selection: a role-based access scheme; an attribute-based access scheme], establish and administer privileged user accounts; (b) Watch privileged role or attribute assignments; (c) Watch changes to roles or attributes; and (d) Take away access when privileged role or attribute assignments are no longer appropriate.

judgment.rationale:
Evidence from both collectors reveals multiple failures against AC-2(7).v3's four sub-requirements:

**(a) Establish and administer privileged accounts per a role/attribute-based scheme:** The endpoint's execution role (`SageMakerExecutionRole-Generic`, evidence c8fab665) carries two wildcard policies — `s3:*` on `*` and `sagemaker:*` on `*`. This is not consistent with a properly administered, least-privilege role-based access scheme. The role name ("Generic") and its overly broad permissions suggest it is not purpose-scoped to this model's actual needs.

**(b) Watch privileged role or attribute assignments:** No evidence of monitoring or alerting on role assignments was found. The CloudTrail record (9aea1ec3) shows a deployment by `data-scientist-jdoe` occurring 2 hours *before* registry approval, indicating that privileged deployment actions are not being gated or watched in real time.

**(c) Watch changes to roles or attributes:** The hotfix `UpdateEndpoint` event (84a87398) was executed by the same IAM user with no corresponding registry entry, meaning changes to the endpoint's operational state are not being tracked against an authoritative change-control record. There is no evidence of automated detection or alerting for such out-of-band changes.

**(d) Revoke access when no longer appropriate:** No evidence of any access revocation workflow, periodic access review, or automated de-provisioning mechanism was found. The broad wildcard permissions on the execution role further suggest that access is never scoped down or revoked as circumstances change.

In summary, all four sub-requirements of AC-2(7).v3 are unmet: the role is over-privileged and generically named, deployments occur before approval (no monitoring gate), hotfix changes bypass the registry (no change-watching), and there is no evidence of access revocation processes.
gaps: No IAM Access Analyzer or AWS Config rule data available to confirm whether role over-privilege is actively detected
No evidence of periodic access reviews or entitlement certification processes (would require HR/ITSM attestation)
No CloudWatch Alarms or EventBridge rules data to confirm whether privileged role changes trigger alerts
No evidence of a formal role/attribute taxonomy or RBAC policy document governing SageMaker execution roles
No evidence of offboarding or de-provisioning workflows for IAM users (e.g., data-scientist-jdoe) when they leave privileged roles

policies.note: Overly broad — training bucket writes and cross-account access not scoped
